XVI.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=16|verse=19}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Thursday in the 2 weeke of Lent.}}There vvas a certaine riche man, & he vvas clothed with purple and silke: and he fared euery day magnifically. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=20}}† And there vvas a certaine begger called Lazarus, that lay at his gate, ful of sores: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=21}}† desiring to be filled of the crommes, that fel from the riche mans table, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''* and no man did give him.''}}∷ but the dogges also came, and licked his sores. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=22}}† And it came to passe that the begger died, and vvas caried {{sup|‖}} of the Angels into {{sup|‖}} Abrahams bosome. And the riche man also died: and he vvas buried in hel. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=23}}† And lifting vp his eies, vvhen he vvas in torments, he savv Abraham a farre of, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Lazarus in Abrahams bosome, and rest: but both in hel, and not in the kingdom of heauen before Christ. ''Hiero. ep. 3. Epitaph. Nepot''.}}∷ and Lazarus in his bosome: {{verse|chapter=16|verse=24}}† and he crying said, Father Abraham, haue mercie on me, and send Lazarus that he may dippe the tippe of his finger into vvater, for to coole my tongue, because I am tormented in this flame. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=25}}† And Abraham said to him, Sonne, remember that thou didst receiue {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ To be in continual pleasures, ease, wealth, peace, and prosperity in this world, is perilous, & a signe of paines in the next. S. Hiero.}}∷ good things in thy life time, and Lazarus likevvise euil: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=26}}† And beside al these things, betvvene vs and you there is fixed {{sup|‖}} a great {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ χάσμα a horrible distance.}}∷ cchaos: that they vvhich vvil passe from hence to you, may not, neither goe from thence hither. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=27}}† And he said, Then, father, I beseeche thee that thou vvouldest send him vnto my fathers house, for I haue fiue brethren, {{verse|chapter=16|verse=28}}† for to testifie vnto them, {{sup|‖}} lest they also come into this place of torments. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=29}}† And Abraham said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Abrahā had knowledge of things in earth which were not in his time. as that they had Moyses and the Prophets bookes vvhich he neuer saw. August. de cura pro mor. c. 14.}}∷ They haue Moyses and the Prophets: let them heare them. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=30}}† But he said, No, father Abraham, but if some man shal goe from the dead to them, they vvil doe penance. {{verse|chapter=16|verse=31}}† And he said to him, If they heare not Moyses and the Prophets, neither if one shal rise againe from the dead, vvil they beleeue.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVI.}}}}

''8. The lord praised.''] This mans deceiuing his maister is not praised, nor vve warranted by his fact to gaine vniustly for to haue wherewith to giue almes: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Good vvorkes.}}but his prudence, in that he prouided so substancially for him selfe vvhilest his maisters goods were in his handes, is commended, not for a vertue, but for a worldly pollicie: and proposed as an example of the careful prouision that rich men (who are Gods stewards in earth) should make for their soules, against they be put out of their bailiship and be called to account, vvhich is the day of their death: and for a condemnation of faithful mens folly and negligence, that being assured they shal out of their offices, and well knovving they might gaine saluation by their money, haue so litle regard thereof.

''9. They may receiue.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Almes meritorious.}}A great comfort to al great almes-men, and a wonderful force and vertue in almes, vvhich beside the merite of the worke of mercie, vvhich (as in other places of Scripture {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Tob. 12, 9. Mat. 25'',}}is said) purgeth sinne and gaineth heauen, pocureth also not onely the praiers of their beadsmen in<noinclude>{{rh|||earth,}}</noinclude>
